### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via deployment.environment (literal, a string literal in buildServeObservability; a string literal in serveOtlpResource), service.instance.id (literal, a string literal in serveOtlpResource), service.name (literal, a string literal in buildServeObservability; a string literal in serveOtlpResource))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 48 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9246279a5103ebfacce7f831c468333d720de17` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b3f9083b27fd6692a4772213343a787a4b0ef2d7` — the merge of head `359a25385aced709a90aefe04654a3bb76b62eaa` into base `c9246279a5103ebfacce7f831c468333d720de17`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b3f9083b27fd6692a4772213343a787a4b0ef2d7 && git checkout b3f9083b27fd6692a4772213343a787a4b0ef2d7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c9246279a5103ebfacce7f831c468333d720de17 359a25385aced709a90aefe04654a3bb76b62eaa && git checkout -B drift-repro c9246279a5103ebfacce7f831c468333d720de17 && git merge --no-ff 359a25385aced709a90aefe04654a3bb76b62eaa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9246279a5103ebfacce7f831c468333d720de17
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c9246279a5103ebfacce7f831c468333d720de17` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4e948efa73297670cf12e421498211504490469e`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed for card #31930: the card body, every comment on it (the seat's Claim 6753763634 and the dev's os-dev-report 6754476552 among them), the seat's Step 0 rulings, the PR #31996 body and file list, and the net diff from merge-base `c9246279` to head (4 files, +203/-5). Nothing was built, run or re-run. Code outside the diff was read with `git show`/`git grep` on `pr-31996` only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Published export: no.** `serveOtlpResource`, `serveInstanceId` and `ServeInstanceHost` are exported from `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, but `@objectstack/cli`'s `exports` map lists only `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body` and `./package.json`. `src/index.ts` re-exports only `default as ServeCommand` from `commands/serve.js`. A deep import of `dist/commands/serve.js` is closed by the exports map, so the new symbols are in-package and not public API.
- **Surface widening: yes, on the OTLP wire.** An exporter declared over `declaresReplicasSharingState(env)` now sends a third resource attribute, `service.instance.id`. This adds a key to what the process publishes to an operator's backend, so it is a widening. Nothing is refused or removed: no env variable, key or route is added or narrowed. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is correct.
- **`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` / detectors: the dev's claim holds.** A `git grep` of `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES|OTEL_SERVICE_NAME|detectResources|envDetector|resourceFromAttributes|@opentelemetry/resources|ResourceDetector` across `packages/cli`, `packages/observability`, `packages/runtime` and `packages/core` finds only the new JSDoc sentence. A `git grep` of `OTEL_` across their `src` finds the same single sentence, and the whole repo has no other `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`. `OtlpHttpMetricsRegistry` (`packages/observability/src/metrics-exporters.ts:189,265-308`) serialises `options.resource` as given and merges nothing else. No operator value exists that the new attribute could override. The PR body, the changeset, the docs and the JSDoc all say this, and no new read is added, as the seat ruled.
- **Step 0 rulings, each held:**
  - The predicate is the existing `declaresReplicasSharingState` (`start.ts:707`, which reads `sharesCloudBindingCredential`, which uses `declaresMultiNode` and requires the redis driver). It is not rewritten, and `declaresMultiNode` is not hoisted.
  - The value is `HOSTNAME-PID`, with a `randomUUID()` fallback when the host name is blank or the call throws.
  - `cluster.nodeId` is not used.
  - There is no override variable.
  - The docs add a paragraph under the Observability table.
  - Both lines read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **R3: the undeclared resource is byte for byte today's.**
  - The builder builds the same object literal as before: `service.name` and then `deployment.environment`, with the same `?? 'objectstack'` and `?? 'production'` defaults, read from `process.env` (passed in as `env`).
  - The third key is added only inside the predicate branch.
  - The CONTROL cases in the new test compare `JSON.stringify` against today's literal for five undeclared shapes, and the dev's ablation A1 shows they catch the attribute appearing on every boot.
  - The diff does not touch the split-brain guard.
- **Hazard review:**
  - **(a) Undeclared bytes: clear.** See R3 above: same key order, no extra key, and the existing attributes are not refactored.
  - **(b) Same-host collision: clear within one PID namespace, with one residual.** Live pids are unique inside a namespace, so two processes on one host (the tested case) get distinct ids. The residual: two replicas that share a host name but run in separate PID namespaces get the same id. Examples are Compose replicas with a pinned `hostname:`, or host-network containers. Both run as pid 1, which the JSDoc itself cites as the restart-stable value. Their metrics would fold back into one series, silently. This is graded under ③ as a should-fix on the claim's wording. It does not block, because the seat ruled the value.
  - **(c) `hostname()` throw: clear.** `try { name = host.hostname().trim(); } catch {}` falls back to `host.randomId()`. Both the blank case and the throwing case are tested.
  - **(d) When the predicate is read: clear.**
    - `buildServeObservability()` has one call site (`serve.ts:4013` at head). It runs after `loadProjectEnvFiles` (`:2459`), so the env is final.
    - The resource is built inside the OTLP branch, immediately before `OtlpHttpMetricsRegistry` is constructed. The exporter's resource is fixed at construction.
    - The same predicate is already asked earlier on the same boot path (`:3466`, the local-database refusal). So the dynamic `@objectstack/cloud-connection` import adds no new failure mode on an undeclared boot. That package is a `workspace:*` dependency of the CLI.
    - Any throw would still land in the existing `init failed; falling back to noop` catch.
  - **(e) `randomUUID` support: clear.** `engines.node` is Node 22.0.0 or later (root and CLI, `.nvmrc` 22), and `node:crypto` `randomUUID` dates from Node 14.17.
  - **(f) What the value exposes: acceptable telemetry practice.** The host name (the pod name on Kubernetes) and the pid are each standard OTel resource attributes in their own right (`host.name`, `process.pid`). They go only to the operator's own configured OTLP endpoint and carry no credential or user data.
  - **(g) Network in the test: clear.** The "wire" cases use an in-process `http` receiver bound to `127.0.0.1:0` (loopback, ephemeral port) and closed in `afterAll`. Nothing leaves the host. The same pattern is used elsewhere in CLI unit tests (`commands/environments/cloud-session.test.ts`).
- **CI on this head (check-runs are the gate verdicts):** 18 success, 15 skipped, 17 in progress, 0 failure or cancelled when read. Still in progress: Type Check (source and consumer gates), Test Core 1/8 through 8/8, six Lint jobs, and Build Docs. The gate verdict is **not yet in**. This contract PASS does not stand in for it, and the head lands only when those runs conclude green.

### ② Semver level

- `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (ruling A) says a changeset's level follows `Metadata-protocol:` alone. `none` covers every non-protocol change and owes `patch`.
- This diff touches no authorable metadata key, value, type or default. It changes a CLI-internal builder and what the OTLP resource carries, so `none` is correct.
- The changeset bumps `'@objectstack/cli': patch`. That matches the level `none` owes.
- The **PR body** carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, each bare at the start of its own line.
- The **changeset** `.changeset/31930-otlp-service-instance-id.md` carries the same two lines with the same values.
- The two carriers agree. No major bump is involved.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev `open_questions`:** none raised.
- **Dev `deviations`: reported as "none". One small undeclared deviation was found.** The ruling asked for one sentence in the docs. The docs hunk is a three-sentence paragraph placed under the Observability table, not in it. It says only what the ruling allows (the condition, the value and the fallback, that no variable exists, and what every other boot exports). Graded **nit**: it is accurate and in scope.
- **Dev `out_of_scope_findings`: escalated to the seat.** The cloud host builds its own OTLP resource in its own observability file and does not get `service.instance.id` from this PR. The dev noted this but did not file it. N5's goal (one series per replica) is not met on the cloud host by this card alone. The seat routes it to cloud#3814 or the `repo:cloud` lane as a carrier item. This does not block this PR, whose scope is `os serve`.
- **should-fix (non-blocking):** `serveInstanceId`'s JSDoc and the changeset say the pid "tells apart two replicas on one host". That holds only inside one PID namespace. Replicas that share a host name but each run as pid 1 in their own namespace get identical ids. Examples are a pinned Compose `hostname:` with replicas, or host-network containers. Either narrow the wording or name this residual in the docs paragraph. The value itself stays as ruled.
- **nit:** the docs addition is a paragraph rather than the ruled single sentence (see above).
- **Security:** none found. No secret or env value is logged or exported.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `359a25385aced709a90aefe04654a3bb76b62eaa`
Local-runs: none

This record covers card #31930 / PR #31996 at head `359a2538`. It is a delta review against this seat's round-1 record on `4e948efa` (PASS). It rests on the net diff from merge-base `c9246279` (4 files, +207/-5), the round-2 delta `git diff 4e948efa..359a2538` (one commit, `359a25385a`), the PR body as it stands now, and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The delta is wording only.** It changes 3 files, +9/-5:
  - in `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, the `serveInstanceId` JSDoc block and nothing else;
  - in `.changeset/31930-otlp-service-instance-id.md`, the first prose bullet;
  - in `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`, the paragraph below the Observability table.

  Every changed line in `serve.ts` is a ` * ` comment line. The code is byte-identical to `4e948efa`: `ServeInstanceHost`, `SERVE_INSTANCE_HOST`, `serveInstanceId`'s body, `serveOtlpResource` and the `buildServeObservability` call site are unchanged. The test file is untouched.
- **The declarations are unchanged.** The changeset front matter (`'@objectstack/cli': patch`) and its `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` lines are outside the delta. The PR body still carries the same two lines.
- **The new wording is accurate.** All three carriers now say the same three things:
  - the pid tells apart replicas that share a host name only within one PID namespace;
  - replicas that share a host name across PID namespaces (a fixed Compose `hostname:`, host-network containers) run as pid 1 and export the same id;
  - the remedy is a distinct host name per replica.

  This matches the code: a namespace-local `process.pid`, joined to the host name. The "each pid 1" phrasing is the common case rather than a guarantee. Under an init shim the pid is some other small number, and the same number in every replica, so the conclusion still holds.
- **Every round-1 judgment carries over, because no code changed:**
  - the new symbols are not a published export (`@objectstack/cli` `exports` and `index.ts` are unchanged);
  - the extra OTLP resource attribute is a widening, correctly declared;
  - nothing in `packages/cli`, `observability`, `runtime` or `core` reads `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` or uses a resource detector, so no operator value exists to override;
  - every Step 0 ruling is followed;
  - R3 holds: an undeclared boot exports today's resource byte for byte, and the split-brain guard is untouched;
  - hazards (a) and (c) through (g) are clear.

  Hazard (b) is unchanged in code. Its residual is now named in all three carriers.
- **CI on this head:** 53 check-runs, all completed. 38 success, 15 skipped, 0 failure, cancelled or in progress. **The gate verdict is green.**

### ② Semver level

`Metadata-protocol: none` owes `patch` under `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (ruling A). The changeset bumps `'@objectstack/cli': patch`. The PR body and the changeset each carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` bare on their own lines, and the two agree. Neither moved in round 2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Round-1 should-fix S1 (the pid claim): RESOLVED.** The fix lands in all three carriers: the `serveInstanceId` JSDoc, the changeset bullet and the docs paragraph. The value is still the seat's ruled `HOSTNAME-PID`.
- **Round-1 nit (the docs paragraph is longer than the one ruled sentence): stands, and is slightly larger.** The S1 fix added a sentence, so the paragraph is now four sentences. Each one is accurate and inside the ruling's scope. It is still a nit.
- **New nit: the PR body is stale.**
  - Line 24 of the "What changes" section still says "the pid tells two replicas on one host apart". That is the unqualified claim S1 narrowed everywhere else.
  - The Verification section still says "All readings on head `4e948efa`".

  The readings still stand on this head, since the delta does not touch code or tests and the check-runs on `359a2538` are green. The body is not a declaration carrier, and both of its declaration lines are intact. Recommendation: the seat patches the body before landing, if the squash commit takes the body. That means narrowing the line-24 sentence to match the changeset and adding one line that carries the readings forward to `359a2538` (prose-only delta). Otherwise the stale claim goes into history.
- **Cloud-host gap: escalated to the seat.** The cloud host builds its own OTLP resource and gets no `service.instance.id` from this PR. The seat routes it in the landing note. It does not block this PR.
- **Dev open questions:** none. **Security:** none.

  - **Value:** `service.instance.id` = `HOSTNAME-PID`, with a `crypto.randomUUID()` fallback when the host name is empty or throws.

  - **R3:** an undeclared boot exports today's two-key resource, byte for byte.
  - **Not exported:** `serveOtlpResource` and `serveInstanceId` stay inside the CLI package.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`, in both the PR body and the changeset.
